# Kona.m

> Explore Kona triathlon race week, IRONMAN World Championship history, 3D bikes, athlete identity, gear, places, stories and an immersive museum.

An independent, unofficial fan and research project. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by World Triathlon Corporation, IRONMAN, Canyon Bicycles GmbH or any referenced athlete or brand. IRONMAN® is a registered trademark of World Triathlon Corporation. Canyon and Speedmax are trademarks of their owners.

## Pages
- [Privacy & data · Kona.m](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/privacy.html): Device storage, optional cloud backup and public account availability.
- [Photo credits · Kona.m](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/credits.html): Source, author, licenses and adaptations for Kona.m photography.
- [Kona.m · Kona triathlon 3D world, bikes & race week](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/): Explore Kona triathlon race week, IRONMAN World Championship history, 3D bikes, athlete identity, gear, places, stories and an immersive museum.
- [Canyon Triathlon Collection · every Speedmax generation, compared](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Canyon_Collection.html): Every Canyon Speedmax generation on record, 1999–2027: interactive 3D exhibits, side-by-side specifications, an aero calculator and a sourced archive of the bikes that were never modelled.
- [Studio · Speedmax Museum — build, paint and share a time-trial bike](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Studio.html): Every bike in the Speedmax Museum and more, in 3D: paint it, give it a film theme, set the scene, dream it in motion and share it. Canyon generations, named machines and studio designs.
- [Speedmax Nights & History Lane · Canyon Speedmax Museum](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Experiences.html): Three night experiences around one Canyon Speedmax (Lava Night, Camp 13 and the Ghost Tunnel) and History Lane, the story from Koblenz in 1985 to Kona. An independent study.
- [About Kona.m · race the version of yourself you haven't met yet](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/about.html): What Kona.m is now, why it exists, what is live, what is still a lab, and what may come next: race identity, bikes, race week, discovery, 3D worlds and the Intern.
- [Kona.m Field Guide · how to play, worlds, bikes & experiments](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/promo.html): A playful public guide to Kona.m: onboarding, tutorials, 3D bikes, worlds, collections, experiments, FAQs and the overworked Intern trying to explain what this app actually is.
- [Canyon Museum — SpeedMax 3.0 (2007)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Speedmax_2007_Museum.html): 3.0 · MY2007 (2007) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax AL 9.0 (2011)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Speedmax_AL_2011_Museum.html): 9.0 · MY2011 (2011) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax CF 9.0 Pro (2011)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Speedmax_CF_2011_Museum.html): 9.0 Pro · MY2011 (2011) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax CFR AXS (2027)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Speedmax_Museum.html): Speedmax CFR AXS (2027) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax CF SLX 8 Di2 (2027)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Speedmax_SLX_Museum.html): Speedmax CF SLX 8 Di2 (2027) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.
- [Canyon Museum — Speedmax Three (2005)](https://joaoccaldas.github.io/konam/Speedmax_Three_2005_Museum.html): Three · MY2005 (2005) — an unofficial, fully procedural Blender model you can explode, ride, inspect and repaint in the browser.

## Facts and sources
- Bikes are unofficial procedural Blender reconstructions calibrated against published photographs and geometry; each exhibit lists its sources and known uncertainties.
- Kona titles on a Speedmax (from museum/kona_champions.json): 2015 Jan Frodeno (Speedmax CF SLX); 2016 Jan Frodeno (Speedmax CF SLX); 2017 Patrick Lange (Speedmax CF SLX); 2018 Patrick Lange (Speedmax CF SLX); 2019 Jan Frodeno (Speedmax CF SLX Disc); 2024 Patrick Lange (Speedmax CFR).
- Brand-room studies: Nike Alphafly 3 in Nike Running Lab (Independent reconstructed study from the public specification. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nike.).
- Photographs are openly licensed (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY / CC BY-SA); authors and licences are shown beside every image.

## Privacy
No account is required. The public web beta uses privacy-minimal first-party session analytics without advertising cookies, account IDs, precise location, raw feedback text or a persistent visitor identifier; the packaged native app does not enable that public-web analytics path. Passport and settings stay local-first. Public email sign-in is currently unavailable. Existing signed-in users may explicitly back up, restore or delete their cloud backup. See privacy.html for the beta data notice and remaining account launch requirements.
